text: Grigol Gegelia - Summoning Pawel Herczynski to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs is another clear proof that this government serves anti-Georgian goals and aspirations (27.04.2026, 12:12)

"The summoning of Herczynski is another clear proof that this government always serves anti-Georgian goals and aspirations," stated Grigol Gegelia, Foreign Secretary of "Lelo - Strong Georgia," regarding the summoning of EU Ambassador Pawel Herczynski.

According to Gegelia, at a time when the ambassadors of Iran and Hungary have not been summoned by the Foreign Ministry, summoning the representatives of Georgia’s strategic partners shows that the “Georgian Dream” government serves to damage the country’s strategic interests.

“At a time when the Iranian ambassador has not been summoned or questioned regarding why he threatened the Georgian people in such a manner; at a time when the Hungarian ambassador has not been summoned or asked about the Russian spy who worked in Georgia for four years—what we were dealing with, whether Hungary was informed, and how we should interpret the fact that a likely Russian spy operated in this city under Hungarian diplomatic cover—in such a situation, Bochorishvili allows herself to attack every ambassador who represents this country's strategic partner states. Whether it is due to statements made regarding Ilia State University or basic pro-democratic remarks, she summons the ambassadors of our country's most important strategic partners for a 'showdown.' This clearly confirms that the so-called government is a hostile administration to Georgia, doing everything in its power to damage our country's national, domestic, and foreign policy interests,” stated Grigol Gegelia.

As a reminder, the EU Ambassador to Georgia, Pawel Herczynski, noted at the European External Action Service in Brussels, where the documentary photo exhibition "Georgia in Focus" was opened, that Georgia is no longer on the right trajectory. According to the Ambassador, "the government has chosen an alternative model of authoritarianism and is distancing Georgia from the European Union."

"Georgia stands at a crossroads. Georgia's future has not yet been written, but what is decided in the coming weeks and months will determine whether Georgia belongs to the family of European nations based on democracy, the rule of law, and human rights, or if it will, unfortunately, return to its dark past. My main message to the Georgian people is: 'Do not lose hope.' We must not allow Georgia and the wonderful, warm, hospitable Georgian people to return to the dark times of violence, civil war, poverty, hardship, and corruption. This is not the future they deserve. As soon as the government expresses a desire to cooperate with us, we will do everything to help Georgia become a member of the European Union," stated Herczynski, whose quote was published by "Netgazeti."
Following the aforementioned statement, the ambassador was summoned to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
